rationale: downstream-chain (lane M3, 2026-09-19, build plan section 6.1 row M3, closing the loop-manifest's population-turn-to-downstream-chain and corpus-turn-to-downstream-chain familyPending hops): this family had a real, wired workflow (.github/workflows/downstream-chain.yml, dated 2026-09-06, chaining tier-opinions/derive-obligations/tag-proposals/apply-classifications then propagation-drain) but no scripts/harness-runs/downstream-chain/ directory and no committed run artifact -- every prior run's outcome was the maintenance family's own posture, a GitHub Actions ephemeral upload-artifact only (this workflow's own header, 'ARTIFACT' section, names that posture deliberately since none of the four scripts it calls are themselves a registered harness family). This registration does not change that: it adds the descriptor and the family directory so a committed downstream-chain-run-NNN.json can exist at all, per this lane's own brief item 5 (amended: register BY DESCRIPTOR ONLY, no edit to any derived list). Governing files mirror maintenance's own precedent (a workflow orchestrator with no single canonical run-*.mjs entry point of its own): the workflow itself (.github/workflows/downstream-chain.yml, whose resolve/gate step and now its own artifact-writer step define what a downstream-chain run is) and the shared composite action every one of its four steps calls (.github/actions/maintenance-step/action.yml, the same action maintenance.yml's own dispatch-one-step job uses). The four scripts this workflow chains (tier-opinions.mjs, derive-obligations.mjs, tag-proposals.mjs, apply-classifications.mjs) stay OUT of this list deliberately, matching maintenance.yml's own convention of not double-counting a step script into two families' governing-file hashes when neither family owns it exclusively today. Paths escape fsi-app/ with '../' since both live at the repo root, one level above fsi-app -- the same escape maintenance's own family.json entry already uses; hashHarnessVersion resolves every entry independently against fsi-app root (baseDir), so this is not order-sensitive.
